# `mm` command reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_skill_cli_reference.py from mind_mem.mm_cli.build_parser().
     Do not edit by hand: tests/test_skill_manual.py fails when this file and the parser disagree. -->

Every subcommand the installed `mm` accepts, with its flags and one example.
The one-line descriptions are the parser's own help text. For *which* command
to reach for, start at [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md); this page answers *how*.

Conventions that hold for every command:

* The workspace is `$MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE`, or the current directory when it is
  unset. Commands that take a `workspace` positional (`anchor`, `chain ...`)
  default to the current directory, so pass `"$MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE"` explicitly.
* Results go to **stdout** (usually JSON); structured logs go to **stderr**.
  Use `2>/dev/null` when piping stdout into a JSON parser.
* `mm <command> --help` prints the same information from the installed version.

A store whose links are broken loads zero records, so `mind-mem-verify` can only say 'compromised'; `survey` says how much and where, and `recover` seals the damaged history and starts a new segment anchored to its sha256. No stored hash is ever rewritten. Subcommands: survey, recover. |

## mm recall

Search memory and print JSON results.

```text
mm recall <query> [--limit LIMIT] [--active-only] [--receipt-envelope] [--since SINCE] [--until UNTIL] [--kernel KERNEL]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<query>` | - |
| `--limit` | - |
| `--active-only` | - |
| `--receipt-envelope` | Wrap the ranked result and its existing serving receipt in an opt-in JSON envelope. |
| `--since` | ISO-8601 lower bound on block Date (inclusive). E.g. --since 2026-01-01. |
| `--until` | ISO-8601 upper bound on block Date (inclusive). E.g. --until 2026-12-31. |
| `--kernel` | Route through a v4 cognitive-kernel strategy instead of plain recall: default, surprise_weighted, lineage_first, contradicts_first, graph_walk. Requires v4.cognitive_kernel in mind-mem.json. Omit for unchanged v3 recall. |

Example:

```bash
mm recall "database decision" --limit 5 --active-only
```

## mm context

```text

```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<query>` | - |
| `--limit` | - |
| `--max-tokens` | - |
| `--receipt-envelope` | Wrap the packed result with its ranked receipt and projection IDs; rendered text is not sealed. |

Example:

```bash

```


## mm review

Batch-review the HITL proposal queue: diff, evidence, approve/reject.

```text
mm review [--json] [--limit LIMIT] [--show PROPOSAL_ID] [--approve IDS] [--reject IDS] [--reason REASON] [--interactive]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output. |
| `--limit` | Show at most N proposals. |
| `--show` | Full detail for one proposal. |
| `--approve` | Comma-separated proposal ids to approve. Each is named explicitly. |
| `--reject` | Comma-separated proposal ids to reject. |
| `--reason` | Rationale for --reject (required, >= 8 characters). |
| `--interactive, -i` | Keyboard session: one keystroke per proposal, then commit. |

Example:

```bash
mm review --json
```

## mm migrate-store

Migrate the workspace block corpus between storage backends.

```text
mm migrate-store --from {markdown} --to {postgres} [--dsn DSN] [--schema SCHEMA] [--dry-run] [--execute] [--with-embeddings] [--embed-model EMBED_MODEL]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--from` | (required) Choices: `markdown`. |
| `--to` | (required) Choices: `postgres`. |
| `--dsn` | Postgres DSN, e.g. "postgresql://mindmem:***@127.0.0.1:5432/mindmem". |
| `--schema` | Postgres schema name (default: "mind_mem"). |
| `--dry-run` | - |
| `--execute` | - |
| `--with-embeddings` | Backfill embedding vectors after the row insert (requires pgvector + Ollama). |
| `--embed-model` | Ollama embedding model name (default: mxbai-embed-large, dim 1024). |

Example:

```bash
mm migrate-store --from markdown --to postgres --dsn "$MIND_MEM_DSN" --dry-run
```

## mm install-all

Auto-detect + configure every installed AI coding client.

```text
mm install-all [--agent AGENT] [--dry-run] [--force] [--no-mcp]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--agent` | Restrict installation to these named agents. Repeat flag for multiple. Default = auto-detect every installed client. |
| `--dry-run` | - |
| `--force` | - |
| `--no-mcp` | Skip native MCP server registration. Default: write both the text hook AND the MCP registration for every agent that supports MCP (Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor, Windsurf, Continue, Cline, Roo, Zed). |

Example:

```bash
mm install-all --dry-run
```

## mm install-model

Download `mind-mem-4b` GGUF (~2.5GB) from HuggingFace and import into Ollama as `mind-mem:4b`. Idempotent.

```text
mm install-model [--model MODEL] [--name NAME] [--dest DEST] [--keep-alive KEEP_ALIVE] [--dry-run]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--model` | GGUF filename on HF. Default: mind-mem-4b-Q4_K_M.gguf |
| `--name` | Ollama tag to register. Default: mind-mem:4b |
| `--dest` | Local path to download into. Default: ~/.cache/mind-mem/ |
| `--keep-alive` | Ollama keep-alive value. -1 = forever (default), 30m, etc. |
| `--dry-run` | - |

Example:

```bash
mm install-model --dry-run
```

## mm doctor

Diagnose workspace state (block-store parity, recall-log schema drift). Add --rebuild-cache or --migrate-recall-log to actually repair.

```text
mm doctor [--rebuild-cache] [--migrate-recall-log]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--rebuild-cache` | Copy Postgres-only blocks into the SQLite recall cache. |
| `--migrate-recall-log` | Add v2-schema columns (intent_type, stage_counts) to the SQLite retrieval_log. |

Example:

```bash
mm doctor
```

## mm token

Federation/HTTP transport token management (rotation primitive).

### mm token rotate

Mint a new token and emit expiry-bearing exports (apply them to the server process environment).

```text
mm token rotate [--length LENGTH] [--grace-seconds GRACE_SECONDS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--length` | Token entropy in url-safe bytes (default 24 = 192 bits). |
| `--grace-seconds` | Grace window during which old tokens remain valid (default 24 h). |

Example:

```bash
mm token rotate
```

## mm import

Import memory from another system into the corpus (local dumps and note directories).

```text
mm import --from {agentmem,chatjson,chroma,letta,markdown,mem0,pinecone,qdrant,weaviate} [<path>] [--endpoint ENDPOINT] [--collection COLLECTION] [--api-key-env API_KEY_ENV] [--text-field TEXT_FIELD] [--page-size PAGE_SIZE] [--max-pages MAX_PAGES] [--max-records MAX_RECORDS] [--max-response-bytes MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES] [--max-total-response-bytes MAX_TOTAL_RESPONSE_BYTES] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--dedup-near] [--dedup-threshold DEDUP_THRESHOLD] [--link-edges] [--dry-run] [--chunk-documents]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--from` | (required) Source format. Note directories: markdown (vault / note tree), agentmem (auto-memory directory). JSON dumps: chatjson (session transcript), mem0, letta, chroma (low value — a vector store keeps embeddings, not source text). Qdrant requires explicit endpoint mode; pinecone/weaviate remain deferred. Choices: `agentmem`, `chatjson`, `chroma`, `letta`, `markdown`, `mem0`, `pinecone`, `qdrant`, `weaviate`. |
| `<path>` | Path to a local dump/tree; omit for endpoint-backed Qdrant imports. |
| `--endpoint` | Qdrant REST endpoint (required for --from qdrant). |
| `--collection` | Qdrant collection (required for --from qdrant). |
| `--api-key-env` | Environment variable containing the Qdrant API key. |
| `--text-field` | Declared Qdrant payload field containing text (default: text). |
| `--page-size` | Qdrant page size, bounded to 100 (default: 100). |
| `--max-pages` | Qdrant page bound (default: 1000). |
| `--max-records` | Qdrant record bound (default: 100000). |
| `--max-response-bytes` | Qdrant response-byte bound (default: 8 MiB). |
| `--max-total-response-bytes` | Qdrant cumulative response-byte bound (default: 64 MiB). |
| `--timeout` | Qdrant per-request timeout in seconds (default: 30). |
| `--dedup-near` | Opt-in (default OFF): collapse near-duplicate records inside the incoming dump using the existing recall dedup cosine layer. Off by default so an import stays a pure function of the dump. |
| `--dedup-threshold` | Cosine threshold used by --dedup-near (default 0.85). |
| `--link-edges` | Opt-in (default OFF): also materialize [[wikilink]] targets as 'cites' lineage edges. Link names are always kept as the block's Links field; this flag only decides whether the lineage graph is written too, so the imported blocks are identical either way. |
| `--dry-run` | Parse and plan the import without writing any block. |
| `--chunk-documents` | Opt-in (default OFF): deterministically chunk markdown/agentmem note trees and stamp UTF-8 source anchors; chunks remain quarantined until governed release. |

Example:

```bash
mm import --from markdown ~/notes --dry-run
```

## mm kinds

v4 block-kind taxonomy (requires v4.block_kinds in mind-mem.json).

### mm kinds backfill

Classify every admitted block into the v4 kind index, and (per their own flags) refresh kind summaries, derive embeddings, and register them for kind-filtered kNN.

```text

```

```bash
mm kinds backfill
```

### mm kinds list

List block ids of one kind, with their full tag sets.


| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--kind` | Kind to list: entity, concept, source, synthesis, image, audio, code, structured, unspecified. |
| `--limit` | Maximum block ids to return (default 100). |

Example:

```bash

```


## mm lineage

Block-lineage subcommands (v3.11.0 typed edges + v3.12 staleness).

### mm lineage flag

Add a typed lineage edge from <src> to <dst> and propagate kind-aware staleness across the dependent subgraph.

```text
mm lineage flag <src> <dst> [--kind {cites,implements,refines,contradicts,supersedes,cooccurrence}] [--weight WEIGHT]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<src>` | Source block id (the new/contradicting block). |
| `<dst>` | Destination block id (the existing block). |
| `--kind` | Edge kind. Default 'contradicts' (the staleness-firing kind). Choices: `cites`, `implements`, `refines`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`, `cooccurrence`. |
| `--weight` | Edge weight (default 1.0). |

Example:

```bash
mm lineage flag D-20261005-002 D-20261005-001 --kind supersedes
```

Install the bundled mind-mem skill (CLI user manual + reference files) into an agent skills directory.

```text
mm skill install [--target TARGET] [--force] [--dry-run]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--target` | Skills directory to install into; the skill lands in <target>/mind-mem (default: ~/.claude/skills). |
| `--force` | Replace an existing, different copy. |
| `--dry-run` | Report what would be copied without writing. |

## mm serve

Launch the mind-mem REST API server (requires mind-mem[api]).

```text
mm serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--allow-unauthenticated-localhost] [--tls-certfile TLS_CERTFILE] [--tls-keyfile TLS_KEYFILE] [--tls-client-ca TLS_CLIENT_CA]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--host` | Bind host (default: 127.0.0.1) |
| `--port` | TCP port (default: 8080) |
| `--allow-unauthenticated-localhost` | v3.7.0 H4: explicit operator opt-in to start the REST API without authentication. Requires a loopback bind (127.0.0.1 / localhost / ::1). |
| `--tls-certfile` | Serve TLS with this certificate chain. The listener is floored at TLS 1.3 — a TLS 1.2 peer cannot complete a handshake. |
| `--tls-keyfile` | Private key for --tls-certfile (when not bundled in it). |
| `--tls-client-ca` | Require client certificates signed by this CA (mutual TLS). Requires --tls-certfile. |

Example:

```bash
mm serve --port 8080
```

## mm http-serve

Launch the v3.9 stdlib HTTP transport (zero dependencies; minimal endpoint surface).

```text
mm http-serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--allow-unauthenticated-localhost] [--tls-certfile TLS_CERTFILE] [--tls-keyfile TLS_KEYFILE] [--tls-client-ca TLS_CLIENT_CA]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--host` | Bind host (default: 127.0.0.1) |
| `--port` | TCP port (default: 8765) |
| `--allow-unauthenticated-localhost` | Bypass token auth when the bind host is loopback. Required for non-token operators; refuses to start without it when no MIND_MEM_TOKEN is set. |
| `--tls-certfile` | Serve TLS with this certificate chain. The listener is floored at TLS 1.3 — a TLS 1.2 peer cannot complete a handshake. |
| `--tls-keyfile` | Private key for --tls-certfile (when not bundled in it). |
| `--tls-client-ca` | Require client certificates signed by this CA (mutual TLS). Requires --tls-certfile. |

Example:

```bash
mm http-serve --port 8765
```

## mm ingest-serve

Serve POST /ingest and drain accepted events into QUARANTINED blocks. Requires v4.ingest_serve in mind-mem.json; off by default.

```text
mm ingest-serve [--port PORT] [--host HOST] [--wal WAL] [--no-wal] [--interval INTERVAL] [--capacity CAPACITY] [--replay-only]
```

| Argument | Meaning |

| `--port` | TCP port to listen on (default: 8788). |

## mm graph-backfill

Extract typed relations from a corpus slice into staged SIGNALS.md proposals. Dry-run by default: prints edges-per-block + predicate histogram (the yield measurement).

```text
mm graph-backfill [--limit LIMIT] [--offset OFFSET] [--write] [--approve SIG-ID] [--list-pending] [--schema] [--reextract-stale] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--limit` | Max blocks to scan (default: 25). |
| `--offset` | Skip the first N corpus blocks. |
| `--write` | Stage extracted edges as pending SIGNALS.md entries for operator review. Without this flag the run is a pure yield measurement. The knowledge graph itself is only written on --approve. |
| `--approve` | Apply the named staged relation signal(s) to the knowledge graph. |
| `--list-pending` | List staged relation signals awaiting approval. |
| `--schema` | Report the live graph schema id, the inputs it is derived from, and how many stored edges were extracted under an older one. |
| `--reextract-stale` | Scan only the blocks behind edges whose schema id is not the live one. On an up-to-date graph this scans nothing. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm graph-backfill --limit 25
```

## mm graph-answer

Answer about an entity using ONLY the k-hop subgraph of governed edges: every claim cites its edge and provenance block, and what the graph does not contain is listed explicitly.

```text
mm graph-answer <entity> [--hops HOPS] [--predicate NAME] [--direction {outgoing,incoming,both}] [--max-triples MAX_TRIPLES] [--include-expired] [--as-of ISO8601] [--context] [--json] [--semantic-required]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<entity>` | Seed entity (any alias; never created if unknown). |
| `--hops` | Subgraph radius (default: 2, max 8). |
| `--predicate` | Restrict to this predicate (repeatable). A predicate with no edges is reported as a gap. |
| `--direction` | Edge direction to follow (default: both). Choices: `outgoing`, `incoming`, `both`. |
| `--max-triples` | Cap on served triples (default: 128). |
| `--include-expired` | Ignore the validity window: also serve edges past their valid_until or not yet at their valid_from. |
| `--as-of` | Evaluate both validity bounds at this instant instead of now (valid-time replay; edges written since still appear). |
| `--context` | Print the serialised triple context instead of the answer. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |
| `--semantic-required` | Require semantic entailment verification; abstain when no verifier is available. |

Example:

```bash
mm graph-answer PostgreSQL --hops 2 --json
```

## mm audit-model

Static security scan of a local model checkpoint. Flags remote-code hooks, unsafe pickle, tokenizer injection. Outputs SHA-256 manifest.

```text

```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<path>` | Path to a local model directory (HF checkpoint layout). |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON instead of text report. |
| `--include-manifest` | Include SHA-256 per-file manifest in output. |
| `--manifest-out` | Write SHA-256 manifest to this path (shasum-compatible format). |
| `--allow-publisher` | Augment the default provenance allowlist with this HF org slug (repeatable). Use for internal fine-tune orgs that aren't in the canonical publisher list. |

Example:

```bash
mm audit-model ./checkpoints/my-model --json
```

## mm sign-model

Sign every file in a local model checkpoint with Ed25519. Writes MODEL_MANIFEST.txt + .sig + MODEL_PUBKEY.pub sidecars.


| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<path>` | Path to a local model directory. |
| `--key-file` | Path to a raw 32-byte Ed25519 private key file. |
| `--generate-key` | Generate a new keypair, write PREFIX.sk (0600) + PREFIX.pub, then sign. |
| `--no-sidecars` | Do not write MANIFEST/.sig/.pub files; print result only. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON instead of human-readable lines. |

Example:

```bash

```

| `--json` | - |

Example:

## mm bind

Attest the current mind-mem.json by writing .spec_binding.json. Until this runs, GovernanceGate's spec-hash check is inert and config tampering is not detected. Exits 3 on drift unless --rebind.

```text
mm bind [--workspace WORKSPACE] [--config CONFIG] [--rebind] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--workspace` | Workspace to bind (default: $MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE or cwd). |
| `--config` | Config to bind (default: <workspace>/mind-mem.json). |
| `--rebind` | Replace an existing binding. Required to attest a config that has drifted — re-binding is an explicit review decision, never automatic. |
| `--json` | - |

Example:

```bash
mm bind --json
```

## mm config

Read/write mind-mem.json. `config set` writes the key and re-attests .spec_binding.json in one step, so a setting change is not read back by GovernanceGate as config tampering.

### mm config set

Set KEY (dotted, e.g. v4.multi_modal.enabled) to VALUE and rebind. VALUE is parsed as JSON when it is valid JSON (true, 500, {...}) and kept as a string otherwise (enforce). Never arms an unbound workspace.

```text
mm config set <key> <value> [--raw-string] [--workspace WORKSPACE] [--config CONFIG] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<key>` | Dotted config key, e.g. governance_mode or proposal_budget.backlog_limit. |
| `<value>` | Value; JSON when parseable, otherwise the literal string. |
| `--raw-string` | Store VALUE verbatim as a string, skipping JSON parsing (for a value like 'true' or '5' that is meant to stay text). |
| `--workspace` | Workspace to configure (default: $MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE or cwd). |
| `--config` | Config to write (default: <workspace>/mind-mem.json). |
| `--json` | - |

Example:

```bash
mm config set governance_mode propose
```

## mm audit-pinned

Run the seven-check audit (and optional Ed25519 verify) on every entry in audit_pinned_models of mind-mem.json. Designed for release CI — non-zero exit on any HIGH finding or verify failure.

```text
mm audit-pinned [--config CONFIG] [--fail-on-missing] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--config` | Path to mind-mem.json (default: ./mind-mem.json). |
| `--fail-on-missing` | Treat a missing pinned path as a hard failure (exit 2). By default, missing paths are skipped with a SKIP marker. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON instead of human-readable lines. |

Example:

```bash
mm audit-pinned --config mind-mem.json
```

## mm anchor

Report corpus blocks that no write scope ever landed, and (with --apply) admit them under a restamp batch. The repair for the unanchored_blocks row of `mind-mem-verify`; content is rewritten unchanged and no status is minted, so anchoring cannot escalate a block.

```text
mm anchor [<workspace>] [--apply] [--limit LIMIT] [--actor ACTOR] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<workspace>` | Workspace path (default: current directory). |
| `--apply` | Open the governed batch and admit the blocks. Without it, nothing is written. |
| `--limit` | Anchor at most this many ids, so a large corpus can be admitted in reviewable passes. |
| `--actor` | Identity to attribute the anchoring to. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm anchor "$MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE" --json
```

## mm chain

Evidence-chain damage census and re-anchor recovery. A store whose links are broken loads zero records, so `mind-mem-verify` can only say 'compromised'; `survey` says how much and where, and `recover` seals the damaged history and starts a new segment anchored to its sha256. No stored hash is ever rewritten. Subcommands: survey, recover.

### mm chain survey

Read the evidence store and report every linkage break. Writes nothing. Exits 1 when damaged.

```text
mm chain survey [<workspace>] [--store STORE] [--limit LIMIT] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<workspace>` | Workspace path (default: current directory). |
| `--store` | Survey this JSONL file instead of <workspace>/memory/evidence_chain.jsonl. |
| `--limit` | List at most this many breaks (0 for all). |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm chain survey "$MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE"
```

### mm chain verify-archive

Re-hash every archive a recovery anchor attests and compare against the sha256 it recorded. Writes nothing. Exits 1 on any missing, unreadable or altered archive, and on a store with no anchors.

```text
mm chain verify-archive [<workspace>] [--store STORE] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<workspace>` | Workspace path (default: current directory). |
| `--store` | Check this JSONL file instead of <workspace>/memory/evidence_chain.jsonl. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm chain verify-archive "$MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE"
```

### mm chain witness

Fix a legacy recovery anchor's companion boundary under explicit operator authority. Prints the witness and its digest; writes nothing until the digest is pinned in mind-mem.json and --confirm is given.

```text
mm chain witness [<workspace>] [--store STORE] --anchor-id ANCHOR_ID --anchor-hash ANCHOR_HASH [--entries ENTRIES] [--authority AUTHORITY] [--trust-assumption TRUST_ASSUMPTION] [--confirm] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<workspace>` | Workspace path (default: current directory). |
| `--store` | Act on this JSONL file instead of the workspace ledger. |
| `--anchor-id` | (required) The exact anchor evidence id. |
| `--anchor-hash` | (required) The exact anchor evidence hash. |
| `--entries` | Companion prefix length the boundary fixes. Defaults to the current chain length; supply it explicitly from an independently established receipt. |
| `--authority` | Authority the witness records. |
| `--trust-assumption` | The explicit assumption. Required, and recorded verbatim. |
| `--confirm` | Append the attestation. Requires the digest already pinned. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm chain witness "$MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE" --anchor-id EV-1 --anchor-hash abc123 --json
```

### mm chain recover

Archive a damaged chain byte-for-byte and start a new segment whose first record anchors the archive's sha256. Prints the census first, always. Refuses on a chain that verifies clean, and writes nothing without --confirm.

```text
mm chain recover [<workspace>] [--store STORE] [--confirm] [--actor ACTOR] [--reason REASON] [--expect-sha256 EXPECT_SHA256] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<workspace>` | Workspace path (default: current directory). |
| `--store` | Recover this JSONL file instead of <workspace>/memory/evidence_chain.jsonl. Rehearse on a copy first. |
| `--confirm` | Actually seal and re-anchor. Without it nothing is archived, replaced or written. |
| `--actor` | Identity recorded in the anchor record. |
| `--reason` | Free text recorded in the anchor's metadata. |
| `--expect-sha256` | Refuse unless the digest surveyed under the append lock matches this reviewed 64-hex SHA-256 pin. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON for the result. |

Example:

```bash
mm chain recover "$MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE"
```

## mm export

Deterministic compliance bundle over the admitted corpus. Two runs over an unchanged corpus produce byte-identical output.


| `--format` | Bundle serialisation. Choices: `jsonl`, `markdown`. |
| `--out` | Write the bundle here ('-' for stdout). With a path, the envelope is printed instead. |

Capture and verify bounded local served-ledger evidence.


| --- | --- |

| `--max-bytes` | Maximum source ledger bytes. |
| `--max-rows` | Maximum source ledger rows. |


### mm receipt verify

Verify a receipt from --input or bounded stdin and print JSON status.

```text

```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--input` | Regular, non-symlink receipt package path. |
| `--stdin` | Read the receipt package from stdin. |
| `--max-package-bytes` | Maximum package bytes read from the file or stdin. |
| `--expected-manifest-sha256` | Optional independently retained manifest digest; mismatch is integrity_failed. |

Example:

```bash

```

## mm recompact

Build a bounded similarity-cluster recompaction proposal (dry-run by default).

```text
mm recompact <block_id> [--workspace WORKSPACE] [--limit LIMIT] [--max-iterations MAX_ITERATIONS] [--min-retention-ratio MIN_RETENTION_RATIO] [--compressor {echo,ollama}] [--model MODEL] [--dream] [--stage] [--actor-id ACTOR_ID] [--actor-role ACTOR_ROLE] [--session-id SESSION_ID] [--tool-id TOOL_ID] [--purpose PURPOSE]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `<block_id>` | Active block ID whose similarity cluster should be re-read. |
| `--workspace` | Workspace to read (default: $MIND_MEM_WORKSPACE or cwd). |
| `--limit` | Maximum similar active blocks to include (1-50). |
| `--max-iterations` | Fixed-point pass bound. |
| `--min-retention-ratio` | Minimum output/source-body ratio. |
| `--compressor` | Local control or explicit local Ollama model. Choices: `echo`, `ollama`. |
| `--model` | Local Ollama model (required for --compressor ollama). |
| `--dream` | Label this opt-in sleep proposal; it is never auto-applied. |
| `--stage` | Stage through propose_update; it is never auto-applied. |
| `--actor-id` | Caller-supplied ActorId for a staged proposal. |
| `--actor-role` | Caller-supplied ActorRole for a staged proposal. |
| `--session-id` | Caller-supplied SessionId for a staged proposal. |
| `--tool-id` | Caller-supplied ToolId for a staged proposal. |
| `--purpose` | Caller-supplied Purpose for a staged proposal. |

Example:

```bash
mm recompact D-20261005-001 --limit 5
```

## mm compliance

Redaction detectors, the pre-write screening door, and the provenance policy.

### mm compliance detectors

List every registered detector. A detector missing here does not exist.

```text
mm compliance detectors [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm compliance detectors
```

### mm compliance scan

Report findings without rewriting anything and without touching the ledger.

```text
mm compliance scan [--file FILE] [--text TEXT] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--file` | Read the text from this path. |
| `--text` | Screen this literal text. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm compliance scan --text "contact alice@example.com"
```

### mm compliance redact

Rewrite findings out of the text and record the pass in the audit chain.

```text
mm compliance redact [--file FILE] [--text TEXT] [--in-place] [--target TARGET] [--agent AGENT] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--file` | Read the text from this path. |
| `--text` | Redact this literal text. |
| `--in-place` | Write the redacted text back over --file. |
| `--target` | Label recorded in the audit entry (defaults to the file path). |
| `--agent` | Actor recorded in the audit entry. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm compliance redact --file notes.md
```

### mm compliance screen

The full pre-write door: provenance policy first, then the detector chain, then the ledger.

```text
mm compliance screen [--file FILE] [--text TEXT] [--actor-id ACTOR_ID] [--actor-role ACTOR_ROLE] [--session-id SESSION_ID] [--tool-id TOOL_ID] [--purpose PURPOSE] [--target TARGET] [--agent AGENT] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--file` | Read the text from this path. |
| `--text` | Screen this literal text. |
| `--actor-id` | ActorId for the pending write. |
| `--actor-role` | ActorRole for the pending write. |
| `--session-id` | SessionId for the pending write. |
| `--tool-id` | ToolId for the pending write. |
| `--purpose` | Purpose for the pending write. |
| `--target` | Label recorded in the audit entry. |
| `--agent` | Actor recorded in the audit entry. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm compliance screen --file notes.md --json
```

### mm compliance provenance

Report the provenance policy and every admitted block that does not satisfy it.

```text
mm compliance provenance [--verbose] [--json]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--verbose` | List every offending block instead of the first 20. |
| `--json` | Emit machine-readable JSON. |

Example:

```bash
mm compliance provenance --json
```

## mm self-update

Check PyPI for a newer mind-mem and upgrade this install.

```text
mm self-update [--check] [--yes] [--pre]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--check` | Report only; exit 10 if an update is available. |
| `--yes, -y` | Upgrade without prompting. |
| `--pre` | Include pre-releases. |

Example:

```bash
mm self-update --check
```
